subject: the Unity suite the roadmap names is built by CMake, which the sealed container does not have; the release's own Makefile runs instead

that Makefile's `make test` compiles cJSON.c and test.c together into one binary rather than linking cJSON.o, so the suite does not judge a substituted object; the units are measured, the suite result is the reference build's
cJSON's numbers are doubles, and the back end refuses floating point, so these units are not expected to pass before the floating-point rung

both units stop in <math.h> before any of their own code is read: the driver defines __GNUC__ 14, so glibc uses GCC 14's built-in vector types, which the front end does not have. With those types supplied by hand the units refuse on floating point instead (cJSON.c: __builtin_nanf undeclared; cJSON_Utils.c: E3101, a function value that is neither an integer nor an object pointer)

sysroot.change: __HAVE_FLOAT32, __HAVE_FLOAT64 and __HAVE_FLOAT32X set to 0
sysroot.why: the TS 18661 _FloatN types are not in the front end's type system, and their prototypes derail the parse of <stdlib.h>

sysroot.change: __HAVE_FLOAT128 set to 0
sysroot.why: same, for _Float128

sysroot.change: the AdvSIMD and SVE guards are forced closed
sysroot.why: the SIMD math prototypes are written in GCC's built-in vector types (__Float32x4_t, __SVFloat32_t), which the front end has no syntax for

sysroot.change: form feeds and vertical tabs are deleted
sysroot.why: C makes both white space (C11 6.4p1); the front end reports a form feed as a stray token, and glibc's regex.h uses one as a page break, which alone refuses every unit that includes it

sysroot.change: renamed out of the search path
sysroot.why: it is a wrapper whose whole body is `#include_next <stdint.h>`, and the front end ignores #include_next, so keeping it hides the C library's real stdint.h and leaves intmax_t undeclared
